title: US State Privacy Laws Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to comply with US state privacy laws including CCPA, Virginia CDPA, Colorado CPA, and more. Protect your data rights today.
intro: US state privacy laws are rapidly evolving, with California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, and Utah leading comprehensive data protection regulations. This checklist helps you understand your rights and take action to protect your personal data under these state laws.

sections.title: Know Your Rights Under State Privacy Laws

items.task: Review your rights under California's CCPA/CPRA
items.why: CCPA gives you the right to know, delete, correct, and opt-out of sale of your personal information from businesses.
items.howTo: Visit the California Attorney General's CCPA page to understand your specific rights. Note that CCPA applies to businesses with $25M+ revenue or handling 100K+ consumers' data.

items.task: Determine which state privacy laws apply to you
items.why: Different states have varying protections. Virginia CDPA, Colorado CPA, Connecticut CTDPA, and Utah UCPA each have unique provisions.
items.howTo: Check your state's consumer protection agency website. Even if your state lacks comprehensive privacy laws, you may be covered by other states' laws if you interact with their businesses.

items.task: Learn how sensitive personal information is protected
items.why: State laws provide enhanced protections for biometric data, health information, precise geolocation, and other sensitive categories.
items.howTo: Review definitions of sensitive personal information in your applicable state law. This typically includes racial origin, health data, sexual orientation, and precise geolocation.

items.task: Submit data access requests to companies
items.why: You have the right to know what personal information companies collect, use, and share about you.
items.howTo: Contact companies directly through their privacy portals or designated email addresses. Most must respond within 45 days. Keep records of your requests and responses.

items.task: Request deletion of unnecessary personal data
items.why: State privacy laws generally grant you the right to request deletion of personal information companies have collected about you.
items.howTo: Submit deletion requests through company privacy portals. Note that businesses can refuse if they need the data for legal compliance, fraud prevention, or completing transactions.

items.task: Opt out of personal data sales and sharing
items.why: Companies often sell or share your data with third parties for advertising and other purposes without explicit consent.
items.howTo: Look for 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' links on websites. Use Incognito Browser to prevent tracking across sites. Submit opt-out requests to data brokers.

items.task: Request correction of inaccurate personal information
items.why: Inaccurate data can affect credit scores, employment opportunities, and other important life decisions.
items.howTo: When you find incorrect information through data access requests, submit correction requests with supporting documentation. Companies must respond within required timeframes.

items.task: Minimize data sharing for targeted advertising
items.why: State laws often require opt-in consent for sensitive data processing and provide rights to limit targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Adjust privacy settings on social media and online accounts. Use Incognito Browser to limit tracking. Enable Global Privacy Control in your browser to automatically opt-out.

items.task: Read privacy policies of services you use
items.why: State privacy laws require companies to provide clear information about data collection and use practices.
items.howTo: Focus on sections about data collection, sharing with third parties, your rights, and how to contact the company. Look for recent updates reflecting new state law requirements.

items.task: Opt out of data broker databases
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell personal information from public records and online sources, often without direct consent.
items.howTo: Research major data brokers like Acxiom, LexisNexis, and Spokeo. Submit opt-out requests through their websites. Consider using automated opt-out services for efficiency.

items.task: Stay updated on new state privacy legislation
items.why: State privacy laws are rapidly evolving, with new states considering comprehensive privacy legislation each year.
items.howTo: Follow state attorney general offices and consumer protection agencies. Subscribe to privacy law newsletters from reputable sources like IAPP or law firms specializing in privacy.

items.task: Keep records of privacy requests and company responses
items.why: Documentation helps track compliance and provides evidence if companies fail to honor your rights under state privacy laws.
items.howTo: Create a simple spreadsheet tracking request dates, company names, request types, response dates, and outcomes. Save email confirmations and response letters.

items.task: Know how to file complaints for violations
items.why: State privacy laws provide enforcement mechanisms when companies don't comply with your privacy rights.
items.howTo: Contact your state attorney general's consumer protection division. For CCPA violations, file complaints with the California Privacy Protection Agency. Document the violation and your attempts to resolve it.
